title: 5.2.25 Vel vs applyForce
description: Why setting .vel every frame fights the physics engine, and when applyForce is the better tool. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is in 5.2.18 (Reading: Forces vs Velocity) and 5.2.19 (Lab: Wind Zone): go back and reread them if you get stuck. Your own everyday words throughout.

Question 1: Why does setting a sprite's .vel directly, every frame, "fight" the physics engine once gravity or other forces are also acting on that sprite? (5.2.18, and your own experience writing the movement code back in 5.1)

Question 2: Describe a situation where you would use applyForce instead of setting .vel directly, and explain why applyForce is the better tool there. (5.2.18 and 5.2.19)

rubric.title: Q1: Explains why .vel fights the physics engine
rubric.description: Student explains that setting .vel directly every frame overrides whatever the physics engine (gravity, applyForce, collisions) already computed for that sprite that frame, so the engine's own influence gets thrown away and re-imposed instead of blending with it. Accept any everyday phrasing of overriding, resetting, or cancelling out the physics engine's own effect; it doesn't need textbook precision. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the part labelled with this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. If the response as a whole is about sprite movement, .vel, applyForce, forces or the physics engine at all, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.

rubric.title: Q2: Describes a real scenario where applyForce is the better tool
rubric.description: Student names a concrete scenario (wind, thrust, a magnet, a continuous push layered on top of gravity, etc.) where applyForce is the better tool, and gives a reason: it respects mass and adds to existing motion instead of replacing it. Credit any situation at all, even loosely worded; a reason, even a vague one, is welcome but not required. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the part labelled with this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. If the response as a whole is about sprite movement, .vel, applyForce, forces or the physics engine at all, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.
